title: Config Change Sentinel: Simulation-based Safe Apply & Revert Assistant
creator: Leila Park
description:
Problem: Configuration changes that affect batching, KV cache policies, or kernel selection can produce large cost regressions or latency spikes if misapplied. Current deploy tooling supports simple rollbacks but lacks an automated, telemetry-driven safety layer that (1) simulates the effective runtime behavior of a config change, (2) applies it in a staged way, and (3) auto-reverts if observed signals cross guardrails.

Goal: Build a 'Config Change Sentinel' microservice and CLI that integrates with the deploy pipeline and Redwood Optimize recommendations to provide a simulation-based preflight, staged apply, continuous monitoring of cost/latency/quality signals, and an automated safe revert path with state snapshots and reconciliation hooks. Emphasis on minimizing false positives, clear operator UX, and extensible guardrail definitions for both hosted and Dedicated/private environments.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight simulator can consume a proposed config diff and produce an execution-level estimate: expected batching size distribution, KV cache hit rate delta, and token-per-second cost delta for top 3 traffic profiles.
Staged apply supports: dry-run, rehearsal (shadow traffic), canary (percent-based), and full roll with automated pause points.

Telemetry-based abort: if latency P95 increases beyond configured threshold OR cost per token increases beyond budgeted delta OR error-rate increases, the sentinel triggers an automated revert and records a causal event.
Revert is safe and idempotent: system snapshots pre-change config, in-flight requests are allowed to finish under original route, and KV cache invalidation is coordinated to avoid cache stampedes.
Console view: per-change timeline with simulator predictions, live telemetry overlay, and one-click ‘force revert’ for SRE/PMs.
Integration tests: end-to-end spec that simulates a bad batching config and asserts sentinel reverts within SLA windows (10m) and publishes root-cause metadata to audit log.
Docs and runbook for on-call with postmortem template and triage checklist.
tasks: Design simulation model for batching + KV-cache interactions (research + small prototype)
Implement sentinel microservice scaffold + API for preflight and apply operations
Add staged apply modes to deploy pipeline and wire sentinel decision hooks
Implement telemetry collector (cost, latency, errors, cache hits) and guardrail evaluator
Implement snapshot + safe-revert workflow with coordinated cache invalidation
Build Console UI mockups and API endpoints for timeline and override controls
Write E2E tests and chaos scenarios (simulate infra flapping + high QPS edge cases)
Prepare runbook and train on-call SREs; publish Confluence doc
guardrails: Latency: route P95 must not increase > 15% over baseline for more than 3 consecutive 1m windows
Cost: estimated token cost delta from simulator must be <= configured budget for change; live cost must not exceed 20% higher than baseline for > 15m
Errors: 5xx rate spike > 0.5% absolute or 200% relative triggers abort
Cache: kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 10 percentage points for primary model triggers investigation
Stability: queue_depth growth > 2x baseline sustained for 5m triggers canary pause
rollback_triggers: Automated: any guardrail violation evaluated by sentinel during canary or live apply
Manual: on-call clicks 'force revert' in Console; must record justification and optional postmortem assignment
Scheduled safety-check failure: periodic reconciliation job detects config drift or partial apply not converged
Policy-based: change lacks required approver signature (SAML/SSO ACL) after 10m into canary -> auto-pause and notify
reconciliation_strategy: Atomic snapshot before apply stored in config-store with versioned key and checksum
Periodic full-state reconciliation job compares desired vs observed config and metrics mapping; reports diffs to audit log
Idempotent revert operation that re-applies snapshot and issues coordinated KV cache warming (shadow-warm) to reduce cold-start effects
Conflict resolution policy: if downstream change happened after our snapshot, abort auto-revert and escalate to human review with suggested diff and timeline
Attach causal metadata (change-id, user, commit, simulator-prediction) to reconciliation events for postmortem
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (research week): small simulator prototype using historical traffic traces and offline replay (2 sprints)
Phase 1 (alpha): sentinel as optional preflight + rehearsal mode for internal infra teams (1 sprint)
Phase 2 (canary): staged apply with 1%, 5%, 25% ramps and automated guardrail checks; enable auto-revert for infra teams (2 sprints)
Phase 3 (beta): enable default for Redwood Optimize suggested batching/caching recommendations for low-risk customers; console controls surfaced (2 sprints)
Phase 4 (GA): full rollout with SLO-backed revert latencies, training, and audit retention (1 sprint)
Post-GA: iterate on simulator fidelity, ML-based prediction of cache-hit deltas, and add per-customer policy profiles
notes: This ticket pairs with a separate UX ticket for Console: PM will file a matching PM-design task after alpha
Simulator should prioritize conservative estimates; false negatives (missed regressions) are costlier than false positives (unnecessary revert), but too many false positives will block adoption
We should reuse existing telemetry infra and tracing hooks to minimize new signal plumbing; budgeted engineering time includes minor schema additions
Consider adding a 'rehearsal' mode where traffic is shadowed to a parallel runtime that applies new config without serving responses to users for higher-fidelity signals
For Private deployments, the sentinel will operate in agent-mode and surface decisions to customer's control plane; we must document RBAC and opt-out flow
